entries.h: What happens if I forget the colored change output?
entries.s: The units you meant to keep are burned. Bitcoin will confirm the transaction normally and nothing warns you. This is the single most expensive mistake in DUST-20.

entries.h: Can I pay the miner fee from my token backing?
entries.s: No. Satoshis that go to the fee are gone, and any units they carried are burned. Always add a separate ordinary bitcoin input to fund the fee.

entries.h: What if two people deploy the same ticker?
entries.s: The first valid deployment wins. Tickers are compared after Unicode NFC normalization and lower-case folding, so "DUST" and "dust" are the same ticker.

entries.h: Malformed integer with a leading zero
entries.s: Integers are strict decimal strings. "0546" is not in strict form even though it parses.
Satoshis are indivisible. Decimal points are rejected outright.
supply must be a positive integer. Zero and negative values are rejected.
A minus sign is not part of a strict DUST-20 integer.
max_sats of 10,000,000,000,000,000 exceeds the 2,100,000,000,000,000 satoshis that will ever exist. The arithmetic is self-consistent but unbackable.
A per-mint cap larger than the entire backing is contradictory.
Tickers exclude whitespace, control characters and the URL delimiters / ? # \ so an identity is always addressable.

entries.s: The mint resolves against the folded identity, so casing does not prevent resolution.

entries.h: Declared sats do not match the deployment ratio
entries.s: 100 units at 546 satoshis is 54,600, not 54,000.

entries.h: Output value differs from declared sats by one satoshi
entries.s: The payload is internally consistent, but the real Bitcoin output holds 54,599 satoshis. The mint is invalid and cannot be repaired after broadcast.
55,146 satoshis exceeds the declared per-mint cap of 54,600.
999,950 units are already minted, so only 50 remain. The mint is rejected in full rather than partially filled.
